geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a courtyard macro around the existing split-wing mass to convert the current notch into a legible public void and ground threshold.
Use a bounded margin to keep the void substantial and occupiable.
Open the court toward the verified access side so the street edge becomes legible and active.
Make the courtyard wrapper the new root so the public void governs the dominant massing while preserving the original split-wing in ancestry.

graph_edits.rationale: Wrap the split-wing datum with a meaningful public void so the ground plane can answer the access edge and satisfy the neighborhood public-space invariant.
Create a usable court-sized subtraction rather than a decorative nick.
Align the new public void to the program-frame access side so the ground threshold reads as a deliberate entry condition.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact split-wing bar with a small central notch/bridge, so it has a recognizable dominant gesture and a basic hierarchy. In four-view terms it is mostly coherent and the parcel containment appears respected, but the massing remains very box-derived and the stepped/void articulation is thin. The thick blue access edge is answered only indirectly: there is a narrow seam and small recess, but not a clearly public ground court or entry figure aligned to the frontage. The roof/section is comparatively flat and generic for a neighborhood-living brief that asks for an active ground threshold and one clear public void or terrace. It is therefore repairable, but not yet program-fit as a convincing neighborhood building mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a hospitality/interior-heavy precedent; useful for threshold and courtyard atmosphere, not for copying program or section logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact courtyard-oriented massing with a legible public threshold and intimate interior-to-exterior transition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Photographic lushness is irrelevant; the transferable value is the open court and edge mediation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Small urban building that opens to a planted void and uses depth/edge thickness to stage publicness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Interior-only reading offers weak massing guidance; good for ground threshold simplicity, not overall form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple, calm interior volume with a clear wall/void relationship and focused occupancy at the ground plane.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a tower precedent with very different scale and typology; only the idea of grounded hierarchy transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked massing can maintain a strong base while varying upper volume.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: too much ramped continuity and looped circulation for this compact bar/split-wing mass; use only as a sectional principle, not a form template.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Continuous sectional gesture and connected terrace/courtyard sequence can organize neighborhood living.

warnings: Visible mass is primarily a simple extrusion split into two blocks; this makes the form legible but underdeveloped for the brief.
Access-edge response is weak: the road frontage is not converted into a strong public void, seam, or terrace.
Section does not yet express a stronger public/upper hierarchy or a meaningful inhabited roof logic.
Candidate is coherent across views, so no hard rejection for view-incoherence; the main issue is semantic/massing under-specification rather than geometry collapse.
